info.bio:
Hay varios artistas con este nombre:

1.Mathangi "Maya" Arulpragasam (Nacida el 18 de julio de 1975 en Hounslow, Londres, Inglaterra) es una artista y cantautora de ascendencia tamil cuyo disco debút "Arular" fue considerado uno de los mejores el año 2005 gracias a sus mezclas de hip hop,dancehall,funk carioca,raggamuffin y electrónica en conjunto con sus agresivas letras de carácter político.

Los conflictos políticos marcaron la vida de M.

mentions.text: …Piracy Funds Terrorism vol. 1, producida durante diez días, que contenía las primeras maquetas de una artista con orígenes en Sri Lanka llamada M.I.A. y que estaba preparando su álbum de debut para XL Recordings. M.I.A. era Mathangi Arulpragasam, hija de un exiliado de la guerrilla tamil de la antigua Ceilán —en su país de origen se le considera un terrorista, un…

mentions.text: …nuevos canales facilitados por internet. El propio título de la mixtape —«La piratería financia el terrorismo»— ya era un indicio del pensamiento de M.I.A., que aseguraba luchar contra la idea del capitalismo como fuerza colonizadora —comprando su mixtape, producto enteramente pirata, financiabas su…

mentions.text: …a la vez que se aprovechaba de esos mismos medios para fortalecer su posición como una de las primeras estrellas del pop global en el siglo XXI. M.I.A. siempre ha sido una figura contradictoria cuyo discurso político ha hecho aguas en múltiples ocasiones, pero musicalmente, y sobre todo en sus dos…

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …dancehall jamaicano, el famoso Bam Bam), hits de R&B, de Madonna y de Prince, y «Walk Like an Egyptian», la icónica canción new wave de las Bangles. M.I.A. presentaba así la fantasía de una aldea global en la que la conexión entre la periferia y el centro se hubiera planteado como una invasión cultural a la inversa: las comunidades empobrecidas del tercer mundo salían de sus reductos y colonizaban el centro —que para M.I.A. era más una articulación a partir de beats de grime, antes que de hip hop— con ritmos excitantes, tan contagiosos como la gripe aviar. En el caso de Diplo y M.I.A., justo desde el principio, se plantea la pregunta de hasta qué punto esta práctica es un homenaje sincero a la música de origen, o un expolio hábil…

podcast.title: Member of the British Empire (2019)
podcast.body: In 2019, M.I.A. was made a member of the British Empire, acknowledging her significant contributions and influence. "And it's interesting that she's also been made a member of the British Empire. That happened in 2019."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Artistic Evolution from Visual Arts to Music
podcast.body: M.I.A. initially began her career as a filmmaker, visual artist, and designer, with her foray into music coming later in her creative journey. "She started as a filmmaker, visual artist, and designer, making music came later."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Background and Refugee Experience
podcast.body: Born Maya Arulpragasam in London, M.I.A. was raised in Northern Sri Lanka after moving there as a child with her parents. Her family was later displaced by the long-running civil war, forcing them to return to London as refugees, an experience that profoundly shaped her artistic perspective and outlook. "Although she was born in London, she was actually raised in Northern Sri Lanka. She moved there as a kid with her parents. But then she and her family were displaced by the long-running civil war, forcing them to go back to London this time as refugees."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Controversial Stances and Mainstream Recognition
podcast.body: M.I.A. faces opposition from factions within the Sri Lankan government and military who hold a negative view of her. She is also critical of mainstream media, despite being named one of the planet's most influential persons by such media in 2009. "There are factions within the Sri Lankan government and military that had a dim view of her. And she's not a big fan of mainstream media. The same mainstream media, the name beer is one of the planet's most influential persons in 2009."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Critique of Authority and Governments
podcast.body: She frequently speaks out against police violence, genocide, and governments that engage in such actions, reflecting her strong political convictions. "MIA has a lot to say about police violence, genocide, and various governments who engage in those sorts of things."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Extensive Activism and Human Rights Advocacy
podcast.body: M.I.A. is a dedicated activist, providing support for Sri Lankan Tamils (her own community), Palestinians, and other people of color. She actively uses social networks to highlight various human rights abuses, often leading to unpopularity with certain groups and even death threats, which she perseveres through. "There's her activism in which she's offered support for Sri Lankan Tammels like her, as well as Palestinians and other people of color. MIA is also found on social networks, highlighting various types of human rights abuse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Fashion Icon and Collaborations
podcast.body: Beyond music, M.I.A. is recognized as a fashion icon, having collaborated with prominent designers such as Marc Jacobs and Versace. "She's also a fashion icon working with Mark Jacobs, Versacee and others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Groundbreaking Nominations
podcast.body: M.I.A. has received numerous awards and achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first person of South Asian descent to be nominated for both an Academy Award and a Grammy. "She's won a number of awards, and she became the first person of South Asian descent to be nominated for both an Academy Award and a Grammy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Philanthropic Endeavors
podcast.body: Her philanthropy extends to building schools in places like Liberia and supporting various forms of pediatric cancer research. "Her philanthropy extends to building schools in places like Liberia. She's also supported various forms of pediatric cancer research."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Themes in Music and Videos
podcast.body: Her music and videos are characterized by their strong social and political commentary, exploring themes such as political violence, identity politics, the plight of immigrants, poverty, sexual and gender stereotypes, and the concept of revolution. "Her music and her videos draw on political violence, identity politics, the plight of immigrants, poverty, sexual and gender stereotypes, and the concept of revolution."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Unexpected Warped Tour Resume Entry
podcast.body: M.I.A. is listed as an artist whose participation in the Warped Tour might be an unexpected or surprising detail on their resume. "Here are some other artists that you may not have expected to have warped on their resume... MIA..."
